Westlands Primary School
Westlands Primary School is a creative learning environment where all children are supported to aim high and achieve their best
Welcome to Westlands Primary School. We are an exciting, forward looking, and innovative school.
Our children are hard-working, enjoy a challenge and love to learn. We provide a huge array of activities for children to broaden their experiences which you will be able to see through our news and updates. Working in partnership with parents, carers and other key members of the community we aim to provide a broad and balanced curriculum for all.
If you want to find out about what we are learning please have a look at our ‘year group’ pages. Paper copies are available on request from the school office.
The website is regularly updated so come back again soon to keep up to date with everything that is going on here at Westlands Primary School!
Victoria Pettett, Headteacher

WESTENBURY '26: The Ultimate Year 6 Send-Off!
WESTENBURY '26: The Ultimate Year 6 Send-Off!
Glastonbury, eat your heart out! On Friday, our incredible Year 6 cohort celebrated the end of their primary school journey in true festival style—and what an absolutely unforgettable party it was!
The weather played along, the music was pumping, and the vibes were immaculate as the entire year group came together to celebrate their hard work, look back on their favorite memories, and dance the afternoon away.
Festival Highlights:
The Main Stage Outdoor Disco: Our field was transformed into a full-blown festival arena. From classic party anthems to some highly questionable staff dancing, the outdoor dance floor was packed from start to finish.
VIP Catering: No festival is complete without a feast! The children enjoyed an endless supply of party food, cold drinks, and plenty of sweet treats to keep their dancing energy levels high.
The Ultimate Headliners: The absolute best part of the day was seeing the entire Year 6 year group together—laughing, posing for photos, and celebrating the brilliant friendships they’ve built over the years.
To our Year 6 Leavers: You have been an absolute joy. Watching you celebrate together yesterday reminded us of just how kind, vibrant, and fun-loving you all are. We are so incredibly proud of the young people you’ve become, and we know you are going to shine in secondary school!

Celebrating Our Students – Birthday Non-Uniform Days from September
Dear Parents, Carers, and the School Community,
At our school, we are always looking for ways to ensure that every single child feels valued, unique, and celebrated. We believe that each student brings something special to our community, and we want to do more to highlight their individuality.
With this in mind, we are delighted to introduce a new tradition starting this September. From the new academic year onwards, we would love to share your child’s birthday with them by inviting them to wear non-school uniform on their special day.
We want this to be a fun, stress-free experience for everyone, so we have put together a few simple guidelines for when birthdays don't fall on a standard school day:
Weekend Birthdays: If your child’s birthday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, they may choose to wear their non-school uniform on either the Friday before or the Monday after their birthday.
School Holidays & Bank Holidays: If their special day falls during the holidays (including the summer break), they are very welcome to choose either the Friday before the holiday starts, or the Monday when we return to school.
Regular School Days: If their birthday is on a normal school weekday, that is their day to shine in their choice of casual clothes!
Please note: There is no cost or donation required for this—this is purely a gift from us to the children to celebrate them as individuals. We only ask that the clothing chosen is safe and appropriate for a normal school day (including practical shoes for playtime).
We are incredibly excited to start this new tradition and look forward to seeing our students celebrate their milestones with an extra splash of colour and personality.
Thank you, as always, for your continued support in making our school a warm, inclusive, and a joyful place to learn.
Westlands Primary School

Forest School Update
Welcome back to a new year of Forest School and outdoor learning!
We kicked off the term with Year 2 (Butterfly and Dragonfly Class), who did a fantastic job alongside our wonderful Year 6 assistants.
Our first week was all about building confidence and refreshing our safety rules to keep everyone safe while exploring:
Stay safe near the fire: Never enter the fire circle.
Respect wildlife: Leave everything growing where it is.
Stay clean: Keep fingers out of mouths while exploring outdoors.
Know your limits: The Blue Rope means stop/no entry.
Even when the heavens opened on Tuesday and left us thoroughly soaked, nothing could dampen the children's enthusiasm! The swings and climbing tree were firm favorites, and everyone loved warming up with delicious hot chocolate during circle time.
Thank you to our Year 6 assistants for being brilliant role models and helping make the first week such a success!

Forest School Update
Our woodland has been buzzing with adventure, learning, and some seriously impressive skills. Here is a look at what our amazing outdoor explorers achieved this week:
Crocodile & Leopard Class: Whittling & Campfires!
Our older adventurers have officially become masters of knife skills! Under careful guidance, they confidently whittled greenwood before rewarding themselves with a classic Forest School treat—toasting S’mores over the campfire!
Safety First: Their safety knowledge was absolutely brilliant.
Growing Confidence: It is wonderful to see their confidence in the outdoor environment grow week by week.
A Huge Thank You: Mrs. Cresswell is incredibly proud of all the children, as well as the fantastic teachers and teaching assistants who came out to support them!
Stay & Play Success!
On Thursday, we welcomed our EYFS children and their grown-ups for a wonderful Stay & Play session.
They had a fabulous time exploring the woods, beautifully supported by our fantastic Year 6 pupils, who did a brilliant job guiding our youngest learners.
Nature's Sweet Treats
To top it all off, the bramble bushes were bursting with ripe blackberries! The children loved foraging and enjoying a sweet, fresh snack (after a thorough wash, of course!).

Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
Safeguarding our children is of paramount importance to us at Westlands Primary School.
We also believe it is essential that children are provided with age-appropriate information to assist them in making sensible choices and developing respect for themselves and others as they progress through the school. Relationships and sex education is learning about the emotional, social and physical aspects of growing up, relationships, sex and human sexuality. As a school we use a scheme of work called Jigsaw (https://www.jigsawpshe.com/) which is a comprehensive programme of PSHE (including RSE) which provides accurate information about the body, puberty and reproduction. It also gives children and young people essential skills for building positive, enjoyable, respectful and non-exploitative relationships and staying safe both on and offline. During the school year we will hold meetings with parents so that there is a clarity about what your children will be learning and we can answer any questions that you may have.
This allows home and school to work together to support our children. Please click on the links below to view our RSE Policy and information booklets regarding the Jigsaw scheme:

Effective communication with parents is one of our main priorities here at Westlands Primary School. We use an App called WEDUC where we send letters home, post important messages and you can log your child's absence.
You will be able to keep up to date with things that have been or are due to happen within the school by logging into the app regularly and you are able to message the main school office via this platform as well.

Breakfast Club
At Westlands Primary School we are passionate about supporting parents, carers and children to have a great start to their day. We believe that when children start their day the right way, they have more energy to learn. We have everything you need that creates a great start to your child’s day with our breakfast club provision. Our breakfast club provides a safe and fun environment where children can start the day having a healthy breakfast, as well as giving them time to socialise and relax, meaning they are emotionally and physically equipped for the day. We are located in the dining hall, accessed via the wooden gate, where children can arrive between 7.30am – 8.30 am. We have a limited number of spaces; therefore, bookings should be requested termly in advance. The Breakfast Club Manager will then be in touch to discuss the space allocation you requested. You can email wps_wraparoundcare@swale.at for any queries. Once a space has been accepted please make your payments to www.parentpay.com account a week in advance. Information
Information
Curriculum
At Westlands Primary School we aim to provide an engaging and exciting curriculum which is built on the foundations of a clear approach to the development of both spoken and written language.
We aim to engage our pupils in deep learning experiences across the curriculum through a clear progression of skills and knowledge coupled with strong links across curriculum subjects and varied learning experiences through enrichment opportunities.
We have a clear approach to the teaching and learning of core subjects, we follow power Maths for maths lessons and have a clear sequence of learning for English lessons. The children are immersed in high quality texts that are linked to their termly topic.
The foundation subjects are taught through clearly sequenced topics that are matched to the interests of the children.
Our curriculum has a clear approach to supporting pupil well-being and providing children with life skills that will help them when they move onto secondary school. We are very lucky to have an on site forest school led by qualified forest school leaders, a swimming pool where children are taught to swim from year 2 - 6 by a qualified swimming teacher and we provide termly food technology lessons.
Curriculum overviews for each year group can be found on the year group webpages.
Please click on each subject to read our curriculum intent and skills progression documents.

Student Life
Student Life
Clubs
Here at Westlands Primary School, we believe in not only the deliverance of high quality PE lessons, but also being able to offer and deliver a range of extra curricular clubs.
These clubs are highly inclusive and appeal to all children. With the variety of sporting events, as well as classroom based clubs, we aim to ensure children are included and are exposed to a variety of opportunities.
We have a qualified dance teacher come in and deliver some high intensity and highly enjoyable street dance lessons to children of all ages.
We utilise all of the space we have, both inside and outside and are able to teach; dodgeball, bench ball, football, rounders, basketball and multi sports.
With classroom based activities including; coding, computing, Lego, colouring and mindfulness.
Our clubs are changed termly and sent out in advance to parents for children to sign up too.
